title: Last N
statement: Implement `solve(events, n)`. `events` is a list of strings. Keep only the last `n` events and return them in arrival order. If fewer than `n` events arrived, return all of them. `n` is at least 0. A bound of 0 returns an empty list.
constraints: Order is oldest-to-newest among the kept events
hints: A deque with maxlen n drops from the left automatically.
Append every event, then return list(deque).
Slicing events[-n:] when n is positive is equivalent. Handle n == 0.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A bounded deque is the structure for a trailing window of events.

editorial: A bounded deque is the structure for a trailing window of events. Append is amortized constant time and the left side falls off once the bound is hit. Taking the tail slice is the same result for a list you already hold. The deque is what you want when the events are a stream.
